discovery.about: The Obscura Rust workspace crates: CLI, CDP server, MCP server, browser page layer, V8 runtime, DOM, networking, renderer, SSRF policy and the embeddable library.
discovery.see: The obscura and obscura-worker binaries: clap global flags (proxy, stealth, robots, user agent, storage dir, private network, V8 flags) and the fetch, serve, scrape and mcp subcommands, fetch dumps, eval and screenshots with adaptive settle, multi-worker serve with ready files, the NDJSON worker protocol, and CLI tests for screenshots, robots, MCP, worker recovery and private-network hints.

The Chrome DevTools Protocol server: discovery endpoints, token-gated WebSocket, thread-per-connection serving with a connection cap, the method dispatcher, domain handlers (Page, Runtime, DOM, Input, Accessibility, Target, Network, Fetch, Emulation, DOMSnapshot, IO, Storage, Browser and the custom LP.getMarkdown), and about 40 regression tests for concurrency, isolation, frames, input and security escaping.

The MCP server for AI agents: about 37 stateful browser tools covering navigation, snapshots, markdown, forms, clicking and typing, waits, evaluation, network and console logs, screenshots, PDF, cookies, storage state and tabs, over stdio or an HTTP transport with body caps, bearer tokens, Origin allowlist and SSE handling.

The Page and BrowserContext layer: navigation with lifecycle levels and chains, subresource and stylesheet loading, evaluation and settling, cookies, storage and browser identity profiles, geolocation override, viewport and full-page screenshots, screencast frames and bounded raster PDF export, plus a fork-only SPA URL adoption patch and tests for binary fetch bodies and unhandled rejections.

The V8 runtime on deno_core: the roughly 800 KB bootstrap.js browser shim implementing Web APIs, Rust ops for DOM mutation, fetch and XHR with interception, per-page runtime state, child frame realms, ES module loading and import maps, document.write streaming, the watchdogs and V8 flag handling, and the startup snapshot build.

The DOM implementation shared by runtime and renderer: DomTree nodes, attributes, shadow roots and form control state with cycle-safe reparenting guards, html5ever parsing including declarative shadow DOM templates, a servo-selectors based CSS selector engine with match caches and an ancestor bloom filter, HTML serialization, and an allocation regression test.

Networking: the reqwest client with an SSRF-guarding DNS resolver and custom trust stores, the wreq and BoringSSL stealth client with Chrome TLS fingerprint, an RFC 6265bis cookie jar, charset detection and decoding, robots.txt cache, the 3,520-domain tracker blocklist and private-network operator hints.

The optional render layer: stylesheet cascade with invalidation, computed style, retained layout over taffy for block, inline, flex, grid, table, float and positioning, cosmic-text inline shaping, tiny-skia paint of backgrounds, borders, text, images, SVG and canvas, bundled fonts, an offline paint binary and a large layout regression suite.

The embeddable Rust library API (Browser, BrowserBuilder, Page, Element, CookieStore) with request interception and preload scripts, an example program, and engine regression tests for frames, isolate teardown, attribute injection, URL resolution, select and textarea semantics, binary XHR and the stealth transport.

The SSRF policy shared by every transport: is_forbidden_ip classifying loopback, RFC 1918, link-local including cloud metadata, and other special-purpose ranges, plus the OBSCURA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK environment opt-in for local testing.
Test-only global allocator wrapper that counts allocation bytes per calling test thread, used by DOM and render tests to assert that traversals do not copy large payloads.
